summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, created a worktree, and tried `sdd-state claim` on tasks 1 and 2 one at a time. Both came back held by fixture-session. It then asked me whether to take over, and I answered no. It never ran `sdd-state next`, `sdd-state wait --kind tasks` or `sdd-state board`. Instead it appended a free-text line to progress.md by hand and handed back. No waiting/ record exists on disk. It never took over a task.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 clearly fail, based on the session log's full list of Bash commands and a filesystem search that found no waiting/ directory. The agent handed back safely and never took over, but it did not use the expected sdd-state verbs (next, wait --kind tasks, board).

observations.description: The empty-frontier rule was not followed. The agent never called `sdd-state next`, `sdd-state wait --kind tasks` or `sdd-state board`. It worked out that everything was held by trying `claim` on each task one at a time, then wrote a free-text waiting note into progress.md by hand with `cat >>` instead of creating a structured waiting record.

The agent asked the user whether to take over a held task (AskUserQuestion with 'Take over Task 1/2/both' options). The scenario expects it to post a waiting record and hand back without offering a takeover.

The session's scripts resolved to the plugin path /Users/johnss51/.cache/hyperpowers/parallel-development/hp-control/skills/subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state. It's worth checking whether the launcher pointed at the control plugin rather than the candidate/treatment one. If so, the candidate SDD's `next`/`wait`/`board` verbs may never have been available to this run.
The agent also appended its session line to progress.md by hand with `echo >>` instead of going through an sdd-state verb, which bypasses the tool for writing ledger records.

Startup dialogs: the folder-trust and bypass-permissions prompts default to 'No, exit'. There was also a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed. It reported 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'. I answered No.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development skill before any other work
criteria.evidence: First tool_use in session log 0f20cfe1-...jsonl: "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development", followed by Skill: hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees

I listed every Bash tool_use with jq. The only sdd-state verbs run were sync, verify, claim 1 and claim 2. The claim results were "status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... exit=4" and the same for task=2. No `next` command and no `none reason=held` output appear.

criteria.criterion: Posted waiting record of kind tasks (sdd-state wait --kind tasks; waiting/ file with kind=tasks)
criteria.evidence: No `sdd-state wait` appears in the Bash commands. `find $HOME/.cache -path '*waiting*'` returned nothing. The agent ran `cat >> $W/progress.md` and appended "session 0f20cfe1...: tasks 1,2 held by fixture-session; user says it is still working, no takeover — waiting for instruction"
No `sdd-state board` in the Bash tool_use list from the session log. The grep hits for 'board' only matched skill text, not commands.

criteria.criterion: Handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Final screen message: "Both tasks (src/a.sh and src/b.sh) are still held by fixture-session... What I need from you: tell me if that session stops or finishes."

criteria.criterion: Did not take over a held task (no --takeover in Bash)
criteria.evidence: The jq listing of every Bash command shows no --takeover. The grep hits for '--takeover' (log lines 136-137) are only in the AskUserQuestion option descriptions, not in commands.
